name: MuddyWater
description: MuddyWater is an Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS)-linked espionage group active since at least 2017, historically focused on government, telecom, and oil & gas targets across the Middle East and North Africa. The group's hallmark is heavy reliance on legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools â€” Atera, ScreenConnect, PDQ, and Action1 â€” abused as off-the-shelf RATs to blend into normal IT traffic. In August-October 2025 the group ran a large phishing campaign from a compromised mailbox via NordVPN, hitting 100+ government entities (embassies, ministries of foreign affairs, consulates) with the new Phoenix v4 backdoor and a Chromium-based credential stealer disguised as a calculator app. Group-IB's February 2026 'Operation Olalampo' disclosure and the appearance of a new Deno-runtime backdoor ('Dindoor') targeting US/Canadian organizations show continued tooling evolution and a slow geographic expansion beyond its traditional MENA focus.

ttps.notes: Malicious Word documents with VBA macros sent from compromised legitimate mailboxes
Lures urge recipients to 'enable content' to trigger macro execution
Abuse of Atera Agent, ScreenConnect, PDQ Deploy/RMM, and Action1 as persistent remote access channels
Phoenix backdoor communicates with C2 over WinHTTP

ttps.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
ttps.notes: Phoenix v4 establishes persistence via Windows Registry modification

ttps.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
ttps.notes: Phoenix copies itself to C:\ProgramData\sysprocupdate.exe; credential stealer disguised as a calculator app
Use of NordVPN and other commercial VPN services to obscure operator infrastructure
Custom Chromium-based credential stealer harvests browser-stored credentials

notable_techniques: Heavy reliance on legitimate, signed RMM software (Atera, ScreenConnect, PDQ, Action1) to evade detection by appearing as routine IT administration traffic
Hijacking of legitimate, already-compromised mailboxes to send phishing from trusted senders rather than spoofed domains
Rapid backdoor iteration â€” Phoenix has progressed through multiple versions (v4 by late 2025) with incremental anti-analysis improvements
Custom credential stealer disguised as a benign calculator utility to avoid triggering user suspicion
Expansion into new runtimes (Deno-based 'Dindoor') signaling active tradecraft modernization beyond traditional VBA/PowerShell loaders
Targets diplomatic and foreign-affairs entities specifically, consistent with Iranian state intelligence-collection priorities
detection_opportunities: Unexpected installation or first-time use of Atera Agent, ScreenConnect, PDQ Deploy/RMM, or Action1 on endpoints that have no prior RMM history
Outbound WinHTTP connections from processes running out of C:\ProgramData with non-standard executable names (e.g., sysprocupdate.exe)
Macro-enabled Office documents originating from previously trusted senders whose mailboxes show anomalous send patterns or sign-ins from VPN exit nodes
New scheduled tasks or registry Run key entries created shortly after a Word document 'enable content' event
Calculator-named or other utility-disguised binaries making outbound network connections or accessing browser credential stores
Egress traffic to known commercial VPN provider ranges (e.g., NordVPN) from servers that should not require outbound VPN connectivity
response_playbook: Inventory endpoints for first-time installation of Atera, ScreenConnect, PDQ Deploy, or Action1 with no prior RMM history.
Review mailbox sign-in activity for anomalous VPN-based access on accounts that recently sent phishing internally.
Hunt for processes running from C:\\ProgramData with non-standard names making outbound WinHTTP connections.
Check for utility-disguised binaries (e.g., a 'calculator' app) accessing browser credential stores.
Look for new Deno runtime installations or executions (Dindoor) as a sign of updated tradecraft.
Scope hunting to diplomatic and foreign-affairs users specifically, given this actor's targeting profile.
